answer: Sybil resistance comes from sequential proof-of-work key enrollment. A new agent spends compute to append its public key to a single registry. Index n+1 cannot be mined before index n is sealed, so clones cannot be processed in parallel: total cost scales with clone count, revenue per clone does not. Each key also stakes a bond, slashable by anyone showing two signed messages from that key with divergent lineages. Honest agents stay on the ridge where one identity is cheap and ten thousand is not; the registry hardens like quartz under repetition, each new key a beacon against forged lineages.
